text: Kafka topics are split into partitions; each partition is consumed by at most one consumer in a group, so parallelism is bounded by the partition count.
An idempotent consumer can process the same message more than once without changing the result, typically by storing a deduplication key such as an event id in Redis before applying side effects.
Change data capture streams row-level changes from a database transaction log to downstream systems, enabling zero-downtime migrations between datastores.
CQRS separates the write model from the read model so each can be scaled and optimised independently, with events keeping the read store eventually consistent.
Caching hot read paths in Redis reduces database round trips; entries need a TTL and an invalidation strategy to avoid serving stale data.
A B-tree index lets PostgreSQL find rows by key in logarithmic time instead of scanning the whole table.
Connection pooling reuses a small set of database connections across requests, avoiding the cost of opening a new connection for every query.
Raft is a consensus algorithm where a leader replicates a log to followers and an entry is committed once a majority of nodes have stored it.
Sharding splits a large table across multiple database nodes by a shard key, so each node holds only a subset of the rows.
With asynchronous replication, a read replica can lag behind the primary, so a client may read stale data right after a write.
A token bucket rate limiter allows short bursts while enforcing an average request rate by refilling tokens at a fixed speed.
Exponential backoff with jitter spaces out retries after failures so that many clients do not hammer a recovering service at the same moment.
Approximate nearest neighbour indexes such as HNSW trade a little recall for much faster similarity search over embeddings.
BM25 ranks documents by term frequency and inverse document frequency with length normalisation, and works well for exact keyword matches.
A cross-encoder reranker reads the query and a passage together and scores relevance more accurately than embeddings, but is too slow to run over a whole corpus.
Online schema migrations add a nullable column first, backfill in batches, then add constraints, so the table is never locked for long.
